transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this pre-filing conference because we have a competitor applying to register the mark NEXORA in classes 9 and 42, covering medical diagnostic devices and software-related services — and they've already begun marketing under that mark. We own an earlier NEXORA registration in the same classes, so the business team wants a measured but effective response. Before I approve the response filing package, I need each of you — trademark, investigations, brand, and conflicts — to report your findings. Let's start with trademark. What have you found regarding our earlier registration and the competitor's application?

transcript.text: Elena, on the brand side, I want to share something important that came up this week. So from a brand strategy perspective, our response should focus on the medical diagnostic device coverage in class 9 and not pursue opposition against the class 42 software-related services. transcript.text: Elena, on the conflicts side, there's a critical issue we need to address before any filing can go forward. Before we can proceed with any adversarial action against the competitor, the competitor-matter team will need to obtain the parent company's informed written consent, and we'll need to establish an ethical screen. I have not yet placed this conflicts clearance result in the filing checklist, and I want to flag that we should not approve the filing package until those steps are completed. I'd recommend we get that consent process initiated immediately so it doesn't bottleneck the enforcement timeline.
